version.changelog:
* Multi-platform refactor: Windows x64 / Windows ARM64 / macOS share one model and delivery layer * macOS support (test build) * Windows ARM64 support + A diagnostic log is written at startup, to make reports easier # Touchpad reverse had no effect on horizontal zoom (regression since 1.7.4, fixed)
---
## Downloads
| Platform | File | Status | |---|---|---| | Windows x64 | `reaper_smoothwheelscroll-x64.dll` | tested | | Windows ARM64 | `reaper_smoothwheelscroll-arm64.dll` | test build, not run on ARM hardware | | macOS Apple Silicon | `reaper_smoothwheelscroll-mac-arm64.dylib` | test build | | macOS Intel | `reaper_smoothwheelscroll-mac-x86_64.dylib` | test build |
Install: put the file for your platform in REAPER's `UserPlugins` folder (`%APPDATA%\REAPER\UserPlugins\` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/REAPER/UserPlugins/` on macOS).
## macOS
**The macOS builds are unverified.** They were compiled and linked on GitHub's macOS runners and export `ReaperPluginEntry` correctly, but no one has loaded them in REAPER yet.
**First run: grant REAPER the Accessibility permission** (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility). Without it the plugin receives no wheel events and behaves as if not installed.
**The log is the diagnostic channel**, and it is on by default on macOS:
open -e "$TMPDIR/SmoothWheelScroll.log"
Its first lines record the build, the REAPER version, whether the wheel hook installed, and whether the master switch is on.
Known gaps on macOS: no settings panel (SWELL provides no window creation there), and surfaces that the Windows build reaches only through its message hook are not animated. Details in `MACOS-PORT.md`.
